definition_en: to get something from a source, or to come from a particular origin
core_image: 一条小溪从岩缝里渗出，顺着山势往下越流越宽
scene: 老师带学生沿河往上游走，最后停在山脚一处小小的泉眼边。Many English words derive from Latin roots.
sceneCN: 这里 derive 指「源自」（第 2 个义项：从某个源头而来）；句意是许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。

senses.title: Get something from a source
senses.definition: to get something such as pleasure, income or knowledge from a particular source
senses.definitionCN: 从某一来源获得乐趣、收入或知识等
senses.example: She derives great pleasure from teaching children.
senses.exampleCN: 她从教孩子这件事上得到很大乐趣。
senses.why: The good thing is not made on the spot; it flows in from somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 好处并非当场造出，而是从别处流进来的。

senses.title: Come from an origin
senses.definition: to come from or have its origin in something
senses.definitionCN: 从某事物而来，以其为起源
senses.example: Many English words derive from Latin roots.
senses.exampleCN: 许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。
senses.why: Every stream can be followed back to the spring that fed it.
senses.whyCN: 每条溪流都能顺水追到供它水的那眼泉。

senses.title: Reach by reasoning
senses.definition: to reach a result by reasoning from facts or rules already known
senses.definitionCN: 依据已知事实或规则推理得出结果
senses.example: We can derive the answer from these two simple rules.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以从这两条简单规则推出答案。
senses.why: Reasoning is a channel cut from known ground to a new result.
senses.whyCN: 推理就是从已知的地面开一条渠，通向新的结果。

intro.en: Derive comes from Latin derivare, to lead water away from a stream, built on de- and rivus, a stream, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: derive 来自拉丁语 derivare，本义是把水从河里引走，由 de- 与 rivus（小河）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Rivus named a stream, and derivare meant to lead its water into a new channel.
items.cn: rivus 指小河，derivare 指把河水引进新的渠道。

items.en: Writers extended it from water to words, arguing that one form flows from another.
items.cn: 作家把它从水移到语言上，说一个形式是从另一个形式流出来的。

items.en: French deriver carried the sense of coming from a source.
items.cn: 法语 deriver 带着「自某处而来」的意思。

items.en: English took it up for both obtaining something and tracing an origin.
items.cn: 英语用它同时表示获得某物与追溯来源。

items.en: Science added the mathematical sense of working a result out from rules.
items.cn: 科学又添上从规则算出结果的数学义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -rive sound, while the meaning group runs from starting somewhere to getting and inferring.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -rive 这一段音，近义组则从发源一路走到获得与推断。

entries.definition: to take something away from someone
a form or thing that comes from another
entries.definitionCN: 由另一形式或事物派生的东西

entries.definition: the origin or formation of a word
to begin to exist in a particular place
to get something that you want
to reach a conclusion by reasoning

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with water leaving a spring and end with a rule that yields an answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从水离开泉眼开始，落到一条算出答案的规则。

normal.en: A river and a word both have a spring somewhere upstream.
normal.cn: 河与词，上游都有一眼泉。

normal.en: To derive is to follow the water back, not to invent it.
normal.cn: derive 是顺着水往回找，而不是凭空造水。

normal.en: Pleasure, profit and meaning can all be led into your own field.
normal.cn: 乐趣、收益与意义，都能被引进你自己的田里。

normal.en: The Latin root rivus is a stream, and the word still flows.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基 rivus 是小河，这个词至今还在流。

normal.en: A formula is a channel dug from known facts to a new result.
normal.cn: 公式就是从已知事实挖向新结果的一条渠。

abstract.en: Picture a hand cupping water where it seeps from rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在岩缝渗水处捧起一汪水。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every small tributary points back to one dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每条小支流都指向同一个点。

abstract.en: Picture a proof written line by line until the last line lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一份证明一行行写下去，直到最后一行落定。

examples.en: Many English words derive from Latin roots.
examples.cn: 许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。

examples.en: She derived great pleasure from teaching children.
examples.cn: 她从教孩子这件事上得到很大乐趣。

examples.en: The formula can be derived from two simple rules.
examples.cn: 这个公式可以由两条简单规则推导出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 derive 记成「得瑞武」：de 像「得」，rive 像「河」，从河里得到水，就是获得与源自。

root: 来自拉丁语 derivare，本义是把水从小河里引走，由 de-（离开）与 rivus（小河）组成，经法语 dériver 进入英语。后来从引水引申为获得好处，又引申为追溯来源与推理推导。

sensesIntro.en: From water led out of a stream, to a word traced to its root, to a result reached by rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把水从河里引出，到把一个词追到词根，再到按规则推出结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stream led out of its old channel into a new one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股水被引出旧河道，流进新渠道。

branches.en: The first sense is what the new channel brings you.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是新渠道带给你的东西。

branches.en: The second sense is the spring that every channel starts from.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是每条渠道起步的那眼泉。

branches.en: The third sense is a channel dug by reasoning alone.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是单靠推理挖出的渠道。

branches.en: Getting and coming from are the two ends of one flow.
branches.cn: 获得与源自，是同一条水流的上下游两端。

branches.en: A word traced to its root and a result traced to its rules use the same backward walk.
branches.cn: 词追到词根、结果追到规则，用的是同一种往回走的步子。

intro.en: Derive has a small Latin family built on a stream and on the act of leading water away.
intro.cn: derive 有一小族拉丁词，建在「小河」与「引水」这两件事上。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin rivus, a stream, and de- adds the sense of away or down.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 rivus（小河），前缀 de- 添上离开、向下的意思。

items.meaning: to lead or draw from a source
items.example: They derive support from old friends.
items.exampleCN: 他们从老朋友那里得到支持。

items.meaning: the act of tracing an origin
items.example: The derivation of the word is unclear.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的来历并不清楚。

items.example: Credit is a derivative of that Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: credit 是那个拉丁动词的派生词。

items.example: The result is derivable from the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果可以从数据推出。

items.example: The drug is derived from a common plant.
items.exampleCN: 这种药是从一种常见植物中提取的。

items.meaning: the act of getting from a source
items.example: He is deriving a new model.
items.exampleCN: 他正在推导一个新模型。
这是一个派生后缀。

items.meaning: in a way that comes from something else
items.exampleCN: 这个术语是派生用法。

definition_en: to move from a higher place to a lower one, or to come down through time
core_image: 石阶一级级往下，尽头没入山谷里的白雾
scene: 山路上天色转暗，石阶湿滑，大家扶着栏杆一步步往下走。The path descends steeply toward the river.
sceneCN: 这里 descend 指「下降」（第 1 个义项：从高处往低处走）；句意是小路陡峭地向河边下降。

senses.title: Move to a lower place
senses.definition: to go down from a higher place to a lower one
senses.definitionCN: 从较高的地方走到较低的地方
senses.example: The plane began to descend through the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机开始穿过云层下降。
senses.why: Gravity offers the easy direction; the body only has to allow it.
senses.whyCN: 重力早已备好省力的方向，身体只需允许它发生。

senses.title: Be passed down
senses.definition: to be handed down from an earlier time or from earlier people
senses.definitionCN: 从更早的年代或更早的人那里传下来
senses.example: The custom has descended from medieval times.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗从中世纪传下来。
senses.why: What comes down a family line arrives the way water comes down a hill.
senses.whyCN: 沿血脉传下来的东西，抵达的方式就像水往山下流。

senses.title: Arrive suddenly in numbers
senses.definition: to arrive suddenly and in large numbers, often in a troubling way
senses.definitionCN: 大批地突然到来，常带有令人不安的意味
senses.example: Reporters descended on the small village overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 记者一夜之间涌进这个小村庄。
senses.why: A crowd can fall on a place the way weather falls on it.
senses.whyCN: 人群扑向一个地方，就像天气压下来一样。

intro.en: Descend goes back to Latin descendere, built from de-, down, and scandere, to climb, and it crossed through Old French into English.
intro.cn: descend 可追到拉丁语 descendere，由 de-（向下）与 scandere（攀爬）构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Scandere meant to climb, so descendere meant to climb down.
items.cn: scandere 指攀爬，因此 descendere 指往下爬。

items.en: The image was always bodily: a foot finding a lower step.
items.cn: 这个意象一直是身体性的：一只脚找到更低的一级台阶。

items.en: Descendre kept both the downward motion and the sense of lineage.
items.cn: descendre 同时保留了向下移动与血统这两层意思。

items.en: English used it for stairs, rivers and family lines alike.
items.cn: 英语把它同样用于台阶、河流与家族世系。

items.en: It now also describes crowds and troubles that arrive all at once.
items.cn: 如今它也形容一下子涌来的大批人与麻烦。

note.en: The look-alike group all carry the -scend or -scent shape, and the meaning group all describe a downward movement.
note.cn: 形近组都带着 -scend 或 -scent 的形状，近义组则都表示向下移动。

entries.definition: the act of going down, or a family line
a person who comes from an earlier family
to behave as if you are above others
entries.definitionCN: 表现得好像高别人一等

entries.definition: to move downward without control
to move quickly to a lower position
to go down slowly below a surface
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢沉到某个表面以下

normalIntro.en: These hooks start on a wet stone stair and end with a crowd pouring into a quiet street.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一级湿滑的石阶开始，落到涌进安静街道的人群。

normal.en: Every stair is a small promise that the ground will rise to meet you.
normal.cn: 每一级台阶都在悄悄保证：地面会升上来接住你。

normal.en: The same word carries a body down and a family name forward.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既把身体送下去，也把姓氏传下去。

normal.en: A crowd descends the way rain does: all at once, from above.
normal.cn: 人群的到来像雨：从上方一下子落下来。

normal.en: Climb up and you ascend; climb down and you descend.
normal.cn: 往上爬是 ascend，往下爬就是 descend。

normal.en: A descendant is simply someone who came down the family stairs.
normal.cn: 后裔不过是从家族那道楼梯走下来的人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding along a cold stone rail.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手沿着冰冷的石栏滑下去。

abstract.en: Picture a valley filling with mist as the path goes lower.
abstract.cn: 想象路越走越低，雾气渐渐填满山谷。

abstract.en: Picture thirty reporters standing at one narrow door.
abstract.cn: 想象三十名记者挤在一扇窄门前。

examples.en: The plane began to descend through the clouds.
examples.cn: 飞机开始穿过云层下降。

examples.en: The custom has descended from medieval times.
examples.cn: 这一习俗从中世纪传下来。

examples.en: Reporters descended on the small village overnight.
examples.cn: 记者一夜之间涌进这个小村庄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 descend 记成「地森得」：de 是向下，scend 像「升」，反过来走，就是往下。

root: 来自拉丁语 descendere，由 de-（向下）与 scandere（攀爬）组成，经古法语 descendre 进入英语。本义是沿台阶往下走，后来用于血统的传承，也形容人或麻烦大批突然到来。

sensesIntro.en: From a foot taking a lower step, to a family line handed down, to a crowd falling on a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只脚踩向更低一级台阶，到一条传下来的血脉，再到扑向某处的人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot finding the next step down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚去找下一级向下的台阶。

chain: A FOOT FINDS A LOWER STEP
A PATH SLOPES TO THE VALLEY
A CROWD FALLS ON A PLACE

branches.en: The first sense is plain downward motion.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是单纯的向下移动。

branches.en: The second sense sends the same motion through time instead of space.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同一种移动从空间移到了时间上。

branches.en: The third sense is motion that arrives all at once, like weather.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一下子到来的移动，像天气那样。

branches.en: Stairs and generations share one picture: each step passes something down.
branches.cn: 台阶与世代共用一幅图：每一级都把东西传下去。

branches.en: A plane and a crowd both leave the height they were at.
branches.cn: 飞机与人群都离开了原来所在的高处。

intro.en: Descend builds a family around going down, family lines and the idea of stepping lower.
intro.cn: descend 长出一族词，围绕向下、血统以及「踏低一级」这个动作。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is scandere, to climb, and de- turns the climb downward.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 scandere（攀爬），前缀 de- 把这次攀爬转向下方。

items.exampleCN: 他们走下窄窄的楼梯。
下山花了两个小时。

items.meaning: one who comes from an ancestor
items.example: She is a descendant of farmers.
items.exampleCN: 她是农民的后代。
他们的后代仍住在这里。

items.example: Put the names in descending order.
items.exampleCN: 把名字按从大到小的顺序排列。

items.example: He would not condescend to explain.
items.exampleCN: 他不肯屈尊解释。
她居高临下的态度让全班不快。

items.meaning: a part that goes below the line
items.example: The letter g has a descender.
items.exampleCN: 字母 g 有一个下伸部分。

definition_en: to say what someone or something is like
core_image: 一个人用手指在空气里勾出轮廓，让旁人看见他脑中的形状
scene: 目击者在警局里回忆那个人的样子，从身高一直说到外套的颜色。She described the man carefully to the police.
sceneCN: 这里 describe 指「描述」（第 1 个义项：用语言说出某人某物的样子）；句意是她向警方仔细描述了那个人。

senses.title: Say what something is like
senses.definition: to say what someone or something is like by giving details
senses.definitionCN: 通过给出细节说出某人某物的样子
senses.example: She described the man carefully to the police.
senses.exampleCN: 她向警方仔细描述了那个人。
senses.why: The speaker lends his eyes to a listener who was not there.
senses.whyCN: 说的人把自己的眼睛借给一个不在场的听者。

senses.title: Call it by a name
senses.definition: to say that something is of a certain kind or quality
senses.definitionCN: 说某事物属于某种类型或具有某种性质
senses.example: He described the plan as a waste of money.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这个计划称作浪费钱。
senses.why: Once you have traced the shape, you can pin a label on it.
senses.whyCN: 轮廓描完之后，就可以在上面别一个标签。

senses.title: Trace a shape through space
senses.definition: to move along a path so that it forms a particular shape
senses.definitionCN: 沿某条路线移动，从而形成一个特定形状
senses.example: The needle described a clean arc on the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 指针在纸上画出一道干净的弧线。
senses.why: A moving thing can write its own outline without a hand.
senses.whyCN: 会动的东西不必用手，也能写下自己的轮廓。

intro.en: Describe comes straight from Latin describere, built on de-, down, and scribere, to write, so its oldest picture is an outline written down.
intro.cn: describe 直接来自拉丁语 describere，由 de-（向下）与 scribere（写）构成，最古老的画面就是被写下来的轮廓。

items.en: Scribere meant to write or scratch marks, and describere meant to copy out a shape.
items.cn: scribere 指书写或刻痕，describere 指把一个形状照样描下来。

items.en: Surveyors used it for marking out land on a map.
items.cn: 测量员用它来表示在地图上标出一块土地。

items.en: English borrowed it for setting down a scene in words.
items.cn: 英语借它来表示用文字把一个场景记下来。

items.en: It gained the weaker sense of calling something by a name.
items.cn: 它又添了一层较弱的用法：给某物安上一个名号。

items.en: Science kept the old geometric sense of a path traced in space.
items.cn: 科学保留了它古老的几何义：在空间里划出的一条路径。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scribe element, while the meaning group all put a scene into words or pictures.
note.cn: 形近组共用 scribe 这一段，近义组则都把场景变成文字或画面。

entries.definition: words that tell what something is like
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物是什么样子的文字

entries.definition: to order a medicine or a rule
to pay to receive something regularly
to show something in a picture or in words
entries.definitionCN: 用图画或文字表现某物

entries.definition: to represent a person or scene in art
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术中表现人物或场景

entries.definition: to make something clear to someone
entries.definitionCN: 使某事物对人变得清楚

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a finger drawing a shape in the air and end with a label pinned on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一根手指在空中画出形状开始，落到别在上面的一个标签。

normal.en: A description is a picture made of words instead of lines.
normal.cn: 一段描述就是用词而不是线条画出的图。

normal.en: If a listener can draw it, the describing worked.
normal.cn: 如果听的人能画出来，这段描述就成功了。

normal.en: De- plus scribere is writing something down from top to bottom.
normal.cn: de- 加 scribere，就是把东西从上到下写下来。

normal.en: To describe a plan as foolish is to hand it a label.
normal.cn: 把一个计划说成愚蠢，就是给它贴上一张标签。

normal.en: A needle can describe an arc with no hand at all.
normal.cn: 一根指针不用手，也能画出一道弧。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing a face in the empty air.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在空里描出一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a list so exact that two strangers pick the same coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一份清单精确到两个陌生人会挑中同一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a museum label that is longer than the object.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比展品本身还长的博物馆标签。

examples.en: She described the man carefully to the police.
examples.cn: 她向警方仔细描述了那个人。

examples.en: The report describes how the money was spent.
examples.cn: 这份报告说明了钱是怎么花掉的。

examples.en: He described the plan as a waste of money.
examples.cn: 他把这个计划称作浪费钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 describe 记成「地斯快布」：de 向下，scribe 是写，把眼前的样子一笔笔写下来，就是描述。

root: 来自拉丁语 describere，由 de-（向下）与 scribere（写）组成。本义是一笔一笔写下来、描出轮廓，后来引申为用语言叙述与形容，也可表示把某物称作什么。

sensesIntro.en: From an outline written down, to a name attached to it, to a path traced by a moving thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被写下来的轮廓，到贴在轮廓上的名字，再到移动之物划出的轨迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tracing an outline that others cannot see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手描出别人看不见的轮廓。

chain: AN EYE TAKES IN A SHAPE

branches.en: The first sense is the outline handed over in words.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是用语言交出去的轮廓。

branches.en: The second sense is the label fixed at the end of the tracing.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是描完之后别上去的标签。

branches.en: The third sense lets the outline draw itself by moving.
branches.cn: 第三个义项让轮廓靠移动把自己画出来。

branches.en: Telling what a thing is like often ends in naming what it is.
branches.cn: 说清一个东西的样子，常常以说出它是什么收尾。

branches.en: Both senses leave a visible line behind, one in words, one in space.
branches.cn: 两个义项都留下看得见的线，一个在文字里，一个在空间里。

intro.en: Describe gathers words about writing an outline down, from a short account to something beyond words.
intro.cn: describe 聚起一族词，都与写下轮廓有关，从简短的叙述到无法用言语形容。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is scribere, to write, and de- adds the sense of writing something down in full.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 scribere（写），前缀 de- 添上「完整写下来」的意思。

items.exampleCN: 把那个房间描述给我听。
这个描述与那个窃贼相符。
这是一个描述性的标题。
这个词是以描述方式使用的。

items.meaning: able to be put into words
items.exampleCN: 这种感觉几乎无法描述。
那景色难以形容。

items.meaning: a word or sign that labels
items.example: Add a descriptor to each file.
items.exampleCN: 给每个文件加一个标识词。
这则广告错误地描述了那套房子。

definition_en: words that tell what someone or something is like
core_image: 一张纸上密密麻麻写着细节，读到的人眼前慢慢浮出画面
scene: 招工启事上列着一长串要做的事，应聘者逐条对照自己会不会。The job description lists every task in clear order.
sceneCN: 这里 description 指「说明文字」（第 2 个义项：逐条说明事物内容的文字）；句意是职位说明把每项任务按清楚的顺序列出。

senses.title: Words that paint a scene
senses.definition: a spoken or written account of what someone or something is like
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面说出某人某物样子的叙述
senses.example: Her description of the village was full of small details.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个村庄的描述满是细小的细节。
senses.why: A good account lets a stranger see a place he has never entered.
senses.whyCN: 好的叙述能让陌生人看见一个从未走进的地方。

senses.title: A written set of details
senses.definition: a piece of writing that explains what something is or how it works
senses.definitionCN: 解释某物是什么或如何运作的文字
senses.example: The job description lists every task in clear order.
senses.exampleCN: 职位说明把每项任务按清楚的顺序列出。
senses.why: Once the picture is fixed on paper, it can be checked and followed.
senses.whyCN: 画面一旦落到纸上，就能被核对、被照着做。

senses.title: A kind or type
senses.definition: a group of people or things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同一类的人或物
senses.example: They sell hats of every description in that shop.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店卖各式各样的帽子。
senses.why: When a kind has no name, people point to the picture it makes.
senses.whyCN: 一类东西没有名字时，人们就指着它呈现的样子来说。

intro.en: Description is the Latin noun descriptio, a drawing or a written copy, formed from de- and scribere, to write.
intro.cn: description 是拉丁名词 descriptio，意为图画或抄本，由 de- 与 scribere（写）构成。

items.en: Descriptio could mean a drawing, a copy or a written account.
items.cn: descriptio 可以指图画、抄本或书面叙述。

items.en: The city planner used it for laying out land on paper.
items.cn: 城市规划者用它来表示在纸上划分土地。

items.en: English borrowed it as the noun standing behind the verb describe.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，作为动词 describe 背后的名词。

items.en: It widened from pictures to any set of stated facts.
items.cn: 它从图画扩展到任何一组被陈述的事实。

items.en: It now even names a type, as in hats of every description.
items.cn: 如今它甚至用来指种类，如各式各样的帽子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the script shape, and the meaning group moves from a spoken account to a rough drawing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 script 这一形状，近义组则从口头叙述一路走到粗略的草图。

entries.definition: to say what something is like
giving a picture in words
a doctor's written order for medicine
a report of an event
a written or spoken statement of facts
entries.definitionCN: 书面或口头的实情陈述

entries.definition: a short rough account or drawing

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand drawing shapes in the air and end with a list of details on paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只手在空中画形状开始，落到纸上的一列细节。

normal.en: A description is a picture made of words instead of lines.
normal.cn: 一段描述就是用词而不是线条画出的图。

normal.en: If a listener can draw it, the description worked.
normal.cn: 如果听的人能画出来，这段描述就成立。

normal.en: De- plus scribere is writing something down from top to bottom.
normal.cn: de- 加 scribere，就是把东西从上到下写下来。

normal.en: A job description writes down what a job will ask of you.
normal.cn: 职位说明写下的，是这份工作会向你要什么。

normal.en: Of every description means the shelf holds all kinds.
normal.cn: of every description 就是说架子上什么种类都有。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing a face in the empty air.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在空里描出一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a list so exact that two strangers pick the same coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一份清单精确到两个陌生人会挑中同一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a museum label longer than the thing it names.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比它所标注的展品还长的标签。

examples.en: The job description lists every task in clear order.
examples.cn: 职位说明把每项任务按清楚的顺序列出。

examples.en: She gave a detailed description of the missing bag.
examples.cn: 她详细描述了那个丢失的包。

examples.en: They sell hats of every description in that shop.
examples.cn: 那家店卖各式各样的帽子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 description 记成「地斯快普神」：de 向下，script 是写，把样子写下来，就成了描述与说明。

root: 来自拉丁语 descriptio，由 de-（向下）与 scribere（写）构成。本义是描画与抄写，指把事物的样子照样记下来；后来指口头的叙述、书面的说明，又引申为种类。

sensesIntro.en: From a picture built in words, to a written sheet of details, to a whole kind of thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从用词搭起的画面，到写满细节的一张纸，再到一整类东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written outline that lets a reader see the thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份让读者看见实物的书面轮廓。

branches.en: The first sense is the scene rebuilt inside a listener.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是在听者心里重建起来的场景。

branches.en: The second sense is the same account fixed on paper for use.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同一份叙述固定到纸上供人使用。

branches.en: The third sense stretches the word from one thing to a whole class.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把词从一件东西拉长到一整类。

branches.en: Spoken and written accounts differ only in where they are stored.
branches.cn: 口头与书面的叙述，差别只在于存放在哪里。

branches.en: A sheet that lists details can also stand for the type it describes.
branches.cn: 一张列出细节的纸，也能代表它所描述的那一类。

intro.en: Description is the noun at the centre of a family about writing things down.
intro.cn: description 是一族词的中心名词，这一族都关于把东西写下来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is scribere, to write, with de- giving the sense of writing out in full.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 scribere（写），前缀 de- 给出「完整写出」的意思。

items.exampleCN: 这个描述与那个窃贼相符。
把那个房间描述给我听。
这是一个描述性的标题。
这个词是以描述方式使用的。

items.meaning: able to be put into words
items.exampleCN: 这种感觉几乎无法描述。
那景色难以形容。

items.meaning: a word or sign that labels
items.example: Add a descriptor to each file.
items.exampleCN: 给每个文件加一个标识词。

items.example: He wore a nondescript grey coat.
items.exampleCN: 他穿着一件不起眼的灰色外套。

definition_en: a large dry area of land with little rain, or to leave someone and never return
core_image: 一片望不到边的沙丘，风把沙脊一条条往前推
scene: 正午的太阳把沙丘照得发白，向导说再走半天也见不到水。Few plants can survive in the desert.
sceneCN: 这里 desert 指「沙漠」（第 1 个义项：干旱少雨的大片沙地）；句意是很少植物能在沙漠里存活。

senses.title: A dry sea of sand
senses.definition: a large area of dry land where almost nothing grows because there is very little rain
senses.definitionCN: 因降雨极少而几乎长不出东西的大片干地
senses.example: Few plants can survive in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 很少植物能在沙漠里存活。
senses.why: Land becomes desert when water stops arriving faster than it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 当水离开的速度一直快过到来的速度，土地就成了沙漠。

senses.title: Leave someone behind
senses.definition: to leave a person or place and never come back
senses.definitionCN: 离开某人或某地且再也不回来
senses.example: He deserted his family and moved to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 他抛弃了家人，搬到另一座城市。
senses.why: To desert is to make a place or a person into empty land.
senses.whyCN: 抛弃，就是把一个人或一个地方变成空掉的荒地。

senses.title: Leave a duty behind
senses.definition: to leave military service or a post without permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许离开军队或岗位
senses.example: The soldier deserted from the army in his second year.
senses.exampleCN: 那名士兵在第二年逃离了军队。
senses.why: The abandoned post is as empty as the abandoned plain.
senses.whyCN: 被丢下的岗位，和那片被丢下的荒原一样空。

intro.en: Desert comes from Latin desertum, something left empty, from deserere, to abandon, built on de- and serere, to join.
intro.cn: desert 来自拉丁语 desertum，意为被丢空的地方，源于 deserere（舍弃），由 de- 与 serere（连接）构成。

items.en: Deserere meant to undo a bond, to leave a thing unjoined and alone.
items.cn: deserere 指把一条联结解开，让某物孤立无依。

items.en: Desertum named any place left empty, not only sand.
items.cn: desertum 指任何被丢空的地方，并不只指沙地。

items.en: French desert carried both the empty land and the act of abandoning.
items.cn: 法语 desert 同时带着空地和舍弃这两个意思。

items.en: English split the two uses between a noun of sand and a verb of leaving.
items.cn: 英语把两种用法分开：名词指沙地，动词指离开。

items.en: Dryness became the main sense, and the verb kept the human one.
items.cn: 干旱成了名词的主要意思，动词则保留了与人有关的那一层。

note.en: The look-alike group is a classic spelling trap, and the meaning group all describe walking away from someone or something.
note.cn: 形近组是典型的拼写陷阱，近义组则都表示离某人某物而去。

entries.definition: sweet food eaten after a meal
empty of people
a person who leaves a duty
to leave someone with no help
to give up someone you should stay with
land that people do not farm or build on
entries.definitionCN: 无人耕种或建设的荒地

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a ridge of sand and end with an empty chair at a table.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道沙脊开始，落到餐桌旁一把空着的椅子。

normal.en: One s is enough for sand; the sweet one takes two.
normal.cn: 沙地一个 s 就够，甜点那个要两个 s。

normal.en: A desert is a place where even leaving leaves a mark.
normal.cn: 沙漠是连离开都会留下痕迹的地方。

normal.en: To desert a friend is to make a small desert of his room.
normal.cn: 抛弃一个朋友，就是把他的房间变成一小片荒漠。

normal.en: Wind works all day and builds only ridges.
normal.cn: 风忙了一整天，只堆出一道道沙脊。

normal.en: Empty land and empty promises share one word.
normal.cn: 空掉的土地与空掉的承诺，共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a boot print that the wind erases before dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个靴印在天黑前就被风抹掉。

abstract.en: Picture a table set for two with one chair pushed in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张为两个人摆好的桌子，一把椅子被推了回去。

abstract.en: Picture a road that stops where the sand begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路在沙地开始的地方断掉。

examples.en: Few plants can survive in the desert.
examples.cn: 很少植物能在沙漠里存活。

examples.en: He deserted his family and moved to another city.
examples.cn: 他抛弃了家人，搬到另一座城市。

examples.en: The village was quite deserted at noon.
examples.cn: 中午时村子里空无一人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desert 记成「得沙漠」：de 像「得」，sert 像「沙地」，走进去就只剩风和沙。

root: 来自拉丁语 desertum，源于 deserere（舍弃），由 de-（解除）与 serere（连接）构成。本义是被解开联结、丢空的地方，后来名词专指干旱的沙漠，动词则保留舍弃与擅离的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a dry plain nobody lives on, to a person left behind, to a duty dropped without leave.
sensesIntro.cn: 从无人居住的干旱平原，到被丢下的人，再到未经许可丢下的职守。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a place stripped of water and of people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被抽走水、也被抽走人的地方。

branches.en: The first sense is emptiness made of heat and sand.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是用炎热和沙堆出来的空。

branches.en: The second sense is emptiness made by a person walking away.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人走开所造成的空。

branches.en: The third sense is the empty post left at the gate.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是门口那个空掉的岗位。

branches.en: Land and people are called deserted by the same logic: no one is there.
branches.cn: 土地与人同样被说成荒废，理由一样：那里没有人。

branches.en: Leaving a friend and leaving a post both break a bond that should hold.
branches.cn: 丢下朋友与丢下岗哨，都断开了本该牵着的那根线。

intro.en: Desert grows a family about empty land and about people who leave their place.
intro.cn: desert 长出一族词，既关于空掉的土地，也关于离开原位的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin serere, to join, and de- undoes the joining, so deserere means to unjoin.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 serere（连接），de- 把这层连接解开，deserere 就是使分离。

items.meaning: to leave behind, or dry empty land
items.example: They crossed the desert by night.
items.exampleCN: 他们在夜里穿越沙漠。
街上空无一人。
他因擅离而受罚。

items.meaning: the act of abandoning a duty
items.exampleCN: 擅离职守曾是很重的罪。

items.example: The deserter was caught at the border.
items.exampleCN: 那名逃兵在边境被抓。
寒带沙漠同样干燥。
过度放牧会使平原沙漠化。
沙漠化威胁着这些农田。

definition_en: to have earned something by what you have done or by what you are
core_image: 天平一端放着多年的付出，另一端等着放下相应的回报
scene: 老工人把最后一颗螺丝拧紧，看也没看墙上的钟。After thirty years of service, she deserves a proper farewell.
sceneCN: 这里 deserve 指「应得」（第 1 个义项：因行为或品质而应当得到）；句意是服务三十年后，她理应得到一场体面的告别。

senses.title: Earn by what you did
senses.definition: to have earned something good or bad by your actions or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 因行为或品质而应当得到好的或坏的结果
senses.example: After thirty years of service, she deserves a proper farewell.
senses.exampleCN: 服务三十年后，她理应得到一场体面的告别。
senses.why: Effort is placed on one pan of a scale, and the reward waits on the other.
senses.whyCN: 付出放在天平一端，回报在另一端等着。

senses.title: Be worth attention
senses.definition: to be important enough to be given attention, help or study
senses.definitionCN: 重要到应当受到关注、帮助或研究
senses.example: This problem deserves a closer look.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题值得更仔细地看一看。
senses.why: Some things ask for our eyes before they ask for anything else.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西先要我们的目光，才谈得上要别的。

senses.title: Be fit for a name
senses.definition: to be good or bad enough to be given a particular label
senses.definitionCN: 好或坏到足以被安上某个名号
senses.example: The little shop deserves the name of a landmark.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小店配得上地标这个称呼。
senses.why: A name is a reward too, and it can be earned or lost.
senses.whyCN: 名字也是一种奖赏，可以被挣得，也可以被失去。

intro.en: Deserve comes from Latin deservire, to serve eagerly, built on de- and servire, to serve, and it passed through Old French.
intro.cn: deserve 来自拉丁语 deservire，意为热心地服务，由 de- 与 servire（服务）构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Servire meant to serve, and deservire meant to serve with full effort.
items.cn: servire 指服务，deservire 指全力以赴地服务。

items.en: By late Latin the serving was done for a reward that was owed.
items.cn: 到晚期拉丁语，这种服务已是为了换取一份欠下的回报。

items.en: Deservir shifted from serving to being worthy of a return.
items.cn: deservir 从「服务」转为「配得上一份回报」。

items.en: English used it for both good and bad outcomes.
items.cn: 英语用它同时指好的与坏的结果。

items.en: It now reaches far beyond service, to praise, blame and attention.
items.cn: 如今它早已超出服务，可用于赞扬、责备与关注。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the serve sound, and the meaning group all say that something is owed to a person.
note.cn: 形近组共用 serve 这一段音，近义组则都表示某人理应得到什么。

entries.definition: rightly given because of what was done
entries.definitionCN: 因所做的事而理应得到的

entries.definition: worthy of help or praise
to leave someone behind
to be worthy of attention or reward
to get something because of your effort
to make something seem necessary

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a scale holding years of work and end with a name that has been earned.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一架盛着多年辛劳的天平开始，落到一个被挣来的名号。

normal.en: A scale does not thank you; it only tells the truth about weight.
normal.cn: 天平不道谢，只说实话，说清两边的分量。

normal.en: Deserve sits one step after do: first the work, then the due.
normal.cn: 先有做事，才有应得，两者差着一步。

normal.en: You can deserve blame as easily as praise.
normal.cn: 该受责备与该受赞扬，道理一模一样。

normal.en: A problem can deserve your eyes before it deserves your money.
normal.cn: 一个问题先值得你的目光，才谈得上值得你的钱。

normal.en: The servant who works hardest earns the rest that follows.
normal.cn: 最卖力的仆人，挣得随后而来的安歇。

abstract.en: Picture an old coin placed on one side of a balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚旧硬币被放到天平的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a name card being handed over after a long wait.
abstract.cn: 想象等了很久之后，一张名牌被递过来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that keeps working after the light has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象灯灭了以后仍在干活的一只手。

examples.en: After thirty years of service, she deserves a proper farewell.
examples.cn: 服务三十年后，她理应得到一场体面的告别。

examples.en: This problem deserves a closer look.
examples.cn: 这个问题值得更仔细地看一看。

examples.en: He finally got the praise he had long deserved.
examples.cn: 他终于得到了早就该得的赞扬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deserve 记成「地服务」：de 像「得」，serve 是服务，服务到位了，就该得到回报。

root: 来自拉丁语 deservire，由 de-（完全）与 servire（服务）组成，经古法语 deservir 进入英语。本义是尽心服务，后来转为因服务而配得回报，再泛化为因任何行为或品质而应当得到好坏结果。

sensesIntro.en: From work that earns a reward, to a problem that earns a look, to a shop that earns a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从挣得回报的辛劳，到值得一看的问题，再到配得上名号的店铺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with effort on one side and its due on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一端是付出，一端是应得。

branches.en: The first sense is the reward that the scale owes.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是天平所欠下的那份回报。

branches.en: The second sense is a smaller due: a look, a hearing, a chance.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是更小的应得：一眼关注、一次倾听、一个机会。

branches.en: The third sense is the largest due: a name that fits.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是最大的应得：一个配得上的名号。

branches.en: A reward and a hearing are both things a person can rightly claim.
branches.cn: 回报与倾听，都是一个人可以正当索要的东西。

branches.en: What deserves attention may also deserve a title.
branches.cn: 值得关注的东西，往往也配得上一个称号。

intro.en: Deserve builds a family around what is owed to effort, and around the negative forms that deny it.
intro.cn: deserve 长出一族词，围绕付出应得的回报，也围绕否定它的反义形式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin servire, to serve, with de- marking service carried through to the end.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 servire（服务），前缀 de- 表示把服务一直做到位。

items.exampleCN: 你该休息一下。
这是一场应得的胜利。

items.meaning: in a way that is fair
items.exampleCN: 她理应感到自豪。
他们帮助值得帮助的学生。
他讨厌那不该由他承担的责备。
这部电影被不该有的遗忘淹没了。
没有人完全不值得帮助。
他得到了应得的赞扬。

definition_en: to plan how something will look or work, or the plan itself
core_image: 桌上摊着一张画满线条的纸，一支笔在纸上落下第一个点
scene: 几个人围着桌子，把草图上的椅子腿改了三遍才点头。They spent a month designing a chair that would fit a small flat.
sceneCN: 这里 design 指「设计」（第 1 个义项：为某物的外形或功能事先作计划）；句意是他们花了一个月设计一把适合小公寓的椅子。

senses.title: Plan a shape before making it
senses.definition: to plan and draw the shape or working of something before it is made
senses.definitionCN: 在动手制作之前计划并画出某物的形状或运作方式
senses.example: They spent a month designing a chair that would fit a small flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们花了一个月设计一把适合小公寓的椅子。
senses.why: The hand tries a thing on paper so that mistakes cost only ink.
senses.whyCN: 手先在纸上试一遍，出错只费掉墨水。

senses.title: The look that was planned
senses.definition: the way something has been planned, shaped or decorated
senses.definitionCN: 某物被规划、造型或装饰出来的样子
senses.example: The carpet has a simple design of leaves and lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地毯有一幅由叶子和线条构成的简洁图案。
senses.why: What began as a plan settles into a visible pattern.
senses.whyCN: 起初只是计划，最后落成看得见的纹样。

senses.title: A purpose kept hidden
senses.definition: a purpose or plan, often one that is not stated openly
senses.definitionCN: 某一目的或计划，常指未明说出来的
senses.example: He asked the question by design, not by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 他问那个问题是故意的，并非偶然。
senses.why: A plan that stays in the head still shapes what the hands do.
senses.whyCN: 留在脑子里的计划，同样会塑造双手的动作。

intro.en: Design comes from Latin designare, to mark out, built on de- and signum, a sign, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: design 来自拉丁语 designare，意为标出，由 de- 与 signum（记号）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Signum was a mark or a sign, and designare meant to mark something out.
items.cn: signum 是记号或标志，designare 指把某物标出来。

items.en: It could also mean to appoint a person or sketch a plan.
items.cn: 它也可以指指定某人，或勾画一份计划。

items.en: Dessigner carried the sense of drawing and intending.
items.cn: dessigner 同时带着画图与打算的意思。

items.en: English used it for a drawing, a plan and a hidden purpose.
items.cn: 英语用它表示图样、计划与隐藏的目的。

items.en: Industry made the drawing sense the dominant one.
items.cn: 工业让「图样」这一层成了最主要的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sign element, and the meaning group all put a shape on paper before it exists.
note.cn: 形近组共用 sign 这一层，近义组则都表示在实物出现前先把形状放到纸上。

entries.definition: to name someone for a duty
a person who plans how things look
secretly planning to get something
to decide in advance how to do something
to write or draw a first rough version
entries.definitionCN: 写出或画出第一份粗略稿

entries.definition: a repeated shape used for decoration

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a pencil dot on blank paper and end with a pattern that repeats on cloth.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从白纸上一个铅笔点开始，落到布上反复出现的花纹。

normal.en: A design is a mistake you are allowed to make on paper.
normal.cn: 设计就是允许你先在纸上犯的那个错。

normal.en: De- plus signum is marking a place so the hand can find it.
normal.cn: de- 加 signum，就是标出一个位置，让手能找到。

normal.en: A chair is designed twice: once in lines, once in wood.
normal.cn: 一把椅子被设计两次：一次用线条，一次用木头。

normal.en: A pattern on a carpet is a plan that decided to stay.
normal.cn: 地毯上的图案，是决定留下来的计划。

normal.en: By design means the accident was never an accident.
normal.cn: by design 就是说那场意外从来不是意外。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil resting on an empty sheet, not yet moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一支铅笔停在空白纸面上，还没有动。

abstract.en: Picture a chair made of thin lines standing in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一把由细线组成、立在空中的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture the same leaf printed across a long roll of cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象同一片叶子印在一长卷布上。

examples.en: They spent a month designing a chair that would fit a small flat.
examples.cn: 他们花了一个月设计一把适合小公寓的椅子。

examples.en: The carpet has a simple design of leaves and lines.
examples.cn: 这块地毯有一幅由叶子和线条构成的简洁图案。

examples.en: He asked the question by design, not by accident.
examples.cn: 他问那个问题是故意的，并非偶然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 design 记成「地赛恩」：de 向下，sign 是记号，把想法一笔笔记成记号，就是设计。

root: 来自拉丁语 designare，由 de-（向下）与 signum（记号）组成，经法语进入英语。本义是标出、画下记号，后来指在制作前规划形状，也指规划出来的图案，还保留着心里的意图这一层。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan tried on paper, to the pattern it leaves, to a purpose kept inside the head.
sensesIntro.cn: 从在纸上试演的计划，到它留下的图案，再到藏在脑子里的意图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn on paper before anything is built.
core.cn: 核心意象：动手之前先落在纸上的一条线。

branches.en: The first sense is the act of drawing the plan.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把计划画出来的那个动作。

branches.en: The second sense is what the plan looks like once it settles.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是计划落定后呈现出来的样子。

branches.en: The third sense is the plan that never becomes visible.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是始终不露面的那份计划。

branches.en: Drawing a shape and the shape drawn are one word apart.
branches.cn: 画形状与画成的形状，只隔着一个词。

branches.en: A plan on paper and a plan in the mind both guide the hand.
branches.cn: 纸上的计划与心里的计划，都在引导那双手。

intro.en: Design gathers words about marking out, planning and the people who do it.
intro.cn: design 聚起一族词，关于标出、规划以及从事它的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin signum, a sign, and de- adds the act of marking something out.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 signum（记号），前缀 de- 添上把某物标出来的动作。

items.meaning: to plan a shape or purpose
items.exampleCN: 她设计简洁的家具。

items.meaning: one who plans how things look
items.example: The designer showed us a sketch.
items.exampleCN: 设计师给我们看了一张草图。
两位设计师分担了这项工作。

items.example: It is a well designed tool.
items.exampleCN: 这是一件设计良好的工具。
设计工作需要耐心。

items.meaning: to plan again in a new way
items.exampleCN: 他们重新设计了整个版面。

items.meaning: to mark out for a duty
items.exampleCN: 他们指定了一间安静的屋子。

items.example: The old designation is still used.
items.exampleCN: 旧的名称仍在使用。

definition_zh: 令人向往的；可取的；有吸引力的
definition_en: worth having or doing because it is good or pleasant
core_image: 橱窗里挂着一件外套，灯光正好落在它的肩上
scene: 看房网站上那套房子照片明亮，采光、楼层和通勤时间都写得很清楚。A quiet street and good light make the flat highly desirable.
sceneCN: 这里 desirable 指「令人向往的」（第 1 个义项：有吸引力、值得拥有）；句意是安静的街道与充足的光线让这套房子非常抢手。

pos.zh: 令人向往的；可取的；有吸引力的

senses.title: Worth wanting
senses.definition: attractive and pleasant enough to be wanted by many people
senses.definitionCN: 有吸引力、令人愉快，因而许多人都想要
senses.example: A quiet street and good light make the flat highly desirable.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的街道与充足的光线让这套房子非常抢手。
senses.why: A thing becomes desirable when imagining it feels better than not having it.
senses.whyCN: 当想着它比没有它更舒服，一件东西就变得令人向往。

senses.title: Worth doing
senses.definition: wise and useful enough to be worth choosing or doing
senses.definitionCN: 明智有用，因而值得选择或去做
senses.example: It is desirable to check the figures twice.
senses.exampleCN: 把数字核对两遍是可取的做法。
senses.why: The same pull works on actions: some choices feel lighter beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 同一种吸引力也作用于行动：有些选择事先就让人觉得更轻松。

intro.en: Desirable comes from Latin desiderabilis, from desiderare, to long for, a word the Romans linked to waiting for a favourable star.
intro.cn: desirable 来自拉丁语 desiderabilis，源于 desiderare（渴望），古罗马人把这个词与等待吉星联系起来。

items.en: Desiderare meant to long for something that was missing.
items.cn: desiderare 指渴望某件尚缺的东西。

items.en: Writers guessed it came from de- and sidus, a star, as in waiting for a good sign.
items.cn: 作家猜测它由 de- 与 sidus（星辰）构成，就像等待一个好兆头。

items.en: Desiderabilis described anything worth longing for.
items.cn: desiderabilis 形容任何值得渴望之物。

items.en: English took the word for things pleasing and worth having.
items.cn: 英语借来这个词，指令人愉快、值得拥有的东西。

items.en: It also grew a cooler sense: advisable rather than attractive.
items.cn: 它又长出一层较冷静的意思：不是说有吸引力，而是说可取。

note.en: The look-alike group all come from desire, and the meaning group ranges from plain attraction to what is wise to choose.
note.cn: 形近组都出自 desire 一族，近义组则从单纯的吸引力一路到明智的选择。

entries.definition: a strong wish for something
in a pleasing or suitable way
entries.definitionCN: 以令人满意或合适的方式

entries.definition: not wanted or not wise
entries.definitionCN: 不受欢迎的或不可取的

entries.definition: pleasant to look at or think about
entries.definitionCN: 看着或想着令人愉快的

entries.definition: sensible and likely to help
better and more worth choosing

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lit shop window and end with a checklist that says this choice is wise.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从亮着灯的橱窗开始，落到一张写着这个选择很明智的清单。

normal.en: Desirable things glow a little before you own them.
normal.cn: 令人向往的东西，在你拥有之前会微微发亮。

normal.en: The word carries desire inside it like a coat carries a lining.
normal.cn: 这个词里头装着 desire，就像外套里缝着内衬。

normal.en: What many people want becomes desirable without being better.
normal.cn: 许多人都想要的东西会变得抢手，未必变得更好。

normal.en: A desirable choice is one that looks lighter the longer you hold it.
normal.cn: 可取的选择，是握得越久越觉得轻的那个。

normal.en: Add un- and the window light goes out.
normal.cn: 加上 un-，橱窗里的灯就灭了。

abstract.en: Picture a coat in a window with one shoulder lit.
abstract.cn: 想象橱窗里一件外套，只有一只肩膀被照亮。

abstract.en: Picture two roads, one of them slightly wider and smoother.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路，其中一条稍微宽一点、平一点。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for a star it cannot touch yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向一颗还够不到的星。

examples.en: A quiet street and good light make the flat highly desirable.
examples.cn: 安静的街道与充足的光线让这套房子非常抢手。

examples.en: It is desirable to check the figures twice.
examples.cn: 把数字核对两遍是可取的做法。

examples.en: Patience is a desirable quality in a teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是教师身上一种令人称道的品质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desirable 记成「地摘若宝」：desire 是渴望，able 是能，能让人渴望的，就是令人向往的。

root: 来自拉丁语 desiderabilis，源于 desiderare（渴望），由 de- 与 sidus（星辰）构成，古人把渴望与等待吉星相连。本义是值得盼望的，后来指有吸引力、令人愉快，也指做事明智可取。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing that pulls the eye, to a choice that quietly recommends itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一件牵住目光的东西，到一个悄悄自我推荐的选项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit object that the eye keeps returning to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件发着光、让人一再回望的东西。

branches.en: The first sense is the pull itself, pleasant and hard to ignore.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那股吸引力，令人愉快，难以忽视。

branches.en: The second sense cools that pull into good advice.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把那股吸引力冷却成一句好建议。

branches.en: A home, a quality and a chance can all wear the same glow.
branches.cn: 一套房子、一种品质、一个机会，都能带上同样的光。

branches.en: Attraction and good sense both answer one question: is it worth having?
branches.cn: 吸引力与明智都在回答同一个问题：它值不值得要。

branches.en: When the answer is no, the same word simply takes un-.
branches.cn: 答案是否定时，这个词加上 un- 就够了。

intro.en: Desirable sits in a family of wanting, with forms for the wish itself and for what should be avoided.
intro.cn: desirable 处在一族表示「想要」的词里，既有愿望本身，也有应当避开的东西。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin desiderare, to long for, and -able adds the sense of being worth that longing.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），后缀 -able 添上「值得被渴望」的意思。

items.exampleCN: 这个地段非常抢手。

items.example: She had a strong desire to travel.
items.exampleCN: 她非常渴望去旅行。

items.example: They discussed the desirability of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们讨论了这个计划的可取之处。
这些房间明亮得令人满意。
这些副作用不受欢迎。

items.example: They noted the undesirability of the site.
items.exampleCN: 他们指出了这个选址的不妥。
这个房间暗得让人不满意。
他得到了期望的结果。

definition_en: a strong feeling of wanting something, or to want it strongly
core_image: 一只手隔着玻璃伸向柜台里的东西，指尖几乎碰到
scene: 孩子贴着玩具店的玻璃站着不动，母亲拉了两次也没拉动。She felt a sudden desire to run out into the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 desire 指「渴望」（第 1 个义项：强烈地想要某物或做某事）；句意是她突然很想跑到雨里去。

senses.title: A strong pull toward something
senses.definition: a strong feeling of wanting to have something or to do something
senses.definitionCN: 想要得到某物或做某事的强烈感受
senses.example: She felt a sudden desire to run out into the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然很想跑到雨里去。
senses.why: The body leans before the mind has finished arguing.
senses.whyCN: 心里还没争出结果，身体已经先倾过去了。

senses.title: Want it strongly
senses.definition: to want something strongly, especially in a formal or polite statement
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要某物，尤见于正式或客气的说法
senses.example: The committee desires a quick answer from the city.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会希望市里尽快给一个答复。
senses.why: The same pull becomes an action when it is spoken as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 同一股拉力一旦用动词说出来，就成了行动。

senses.title: The thing itself wished for
senses.definition: the particular thing that a person wishes to have
senses.definitionCN: 某人所希望得到的那样具体的东西
senses.example: Her one desire was a small house near the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 她唯一的心愿是海边的一座小房子。
senses.why: A feeling can harden into a single object the mind keeps pointing at.
senses.whyCN: 一种感受会凝固成一个具体的物件，让心思一直指着它。

intro.en: Desire comes from Latin desiderare, to long for, which Roman writers linked to de- and sidus, a star, as if waiting for a favourable sign.
intro.cn: desire 来自拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），罗马作家把它与 de- 和 sidus（星辰）相连，仿佛是等待一个吉兆。

items.en: Desiderare named the ache for something absent.
items.cn: desiderare 指对缺席之物的那种惦念。

items.en: The old guess was de- plus sidus, to stop looking at the stars and wait for one.
items.cn: 旧时的猜测是 de- 加 sidus，意为不再张望群星，只等那一颗。

items.en: Desirer carried the feeling into the language of court and prayer.
items.cn: desirer 把这股感受带进宫廷与祈祷的语言。

items.en: English used it for both holy longing and plain appetite.
items.cn: 英语用它兼指神圣的向往与普通的欲求。

items.en: It now covers everything from a wish for rain to a formal request.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖从盼一场雨到一份正式请求的一切。

note.en: The look-alike group all belong to the desire family, and the meaning group moves from quiet longing to sharp craving.
note.cn: 形近组都属于 desire 这一族，近义组则从安静的向往走到尖锐的渴求。

entries.definition: worth wanting
feeling a wish for something
not wanted at all
a deep and lasting wish
a very strong need for something
a hope for something to happen

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand pressed to shop glass and end with one small house by the sea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只手贴在商店玻璃上开始，落到海边的一座小房子。

normal.en: Desire is a hand that has already moved before permission arrives.
normal.cn: 渴望是一只手，许可还没到，它已经先动了。

normal.en: The old Romans heard a star inside the word.
normal.cn: 古罗马人从这个词里听见了一颗星。

normal.en: A wish can be quiet; a desire leans hard on the door.
normal.cn: 心愿可以很轻，渴望却会用力顶住那扇门。

normal.en: What you desire is often the shape your lack has taken.
normal.cn: 你所渴望的，常常就是你的缺失长成的形状。

normal.en: One desire, one object: the feeling narrows to a point.
normal.cn: 一种渴望，一个对象：感受收窄成一个点。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip almost touching the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖几乎贴到玻璃上。

abstract.en: Picture a small house with one lit window above the water.
abstract.cn: 想象水面上方一座亮着一扇窗的小房子。

abstract.en: Picture a star that will not come closer no matter how long you watch.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗无论看多久都不会靠近的星。

examples.en: She felt a sudden desire to run out into the rain.
examples.cn: 她突然很想跑到雨里去。

examples.en: The committee desires a quick answer from the city.
examples.cn: 委员会希望市里尽快给一个答复。

examples.en: Her one desire was a small house near the sea.
examples.cn: 她唯一的心愿是海边的一座小房子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desire 记成「地摘尔」：de 向下，sire 像「伸手」，手一直往下伸，是想抓住渴望的东西。

root: 来自拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），由 de- 与 sidus（星辰）构成，古人把这份心情与等待吉星相连。本义是对缺席之物的惦念，后来兼指强烈的愿望、正式表达的想要，以及所盼望的那件具体东西。

sensesIntro.en: From a pull toward what is absent, to the act of wanting it aloud, to the one thing pointed at.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对缺席之物的牵引，到把想要说出口的动作，再到被指着的那一件东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching toward something behind glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向玻璃后面的东西。

branches.en: The first sense is the pull itself, before any object is named.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那股牵引本身，还没有点明对象。

branches.en: The second sense is the pull spoken aloud as a verb.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把那股牵引用动词说出口。

branches.en: The third sense is the single thing at the end of the reach.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是伸出去的手最终指着的那件东西。

branches.en: Feeling and asking are the same force at two volumes.
branches.cn: 感受与请求，是同一种力道的一轻一重。

branches.en: To desire something is to let one object fill the whole view.
branches.cn: 想要某物，就是让一件东西占满整个视野。

intro.en: Desire gathers a family about wanting, from the quality of being worth wanting to the state of not being wanted.
intro.cn: desire 聚起一族表示「想要」的词，从值得想要的性质到不被想要的状态。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin desiderare, to long for, and the family adds endings for quality, manner and negation.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），这一族用后缀添上性质、方式与否定。

items.example: He had no desire to argue.
items.exampleCN: 他毫无争辩的意愿。
她的愿望随年龄而变。
他得到了期望的效果。

items.example: Those desiring tickets should write in.
items.exampleCN: 想要票的人请来信。
这个地段非常抢手。

items.meaning: full of a wish for something
items.exampleCN: 他们渴望和平。
他们质疑它是否可取。
这项变动带来了不想要的成本。

definition_en: a table used for writing or working, often with drawers
core_image: 靠窗一张木桌，桌面被手肘磨出一块发浅的地方
scene: 清晨的办公室只亮着一盏灯，桌上摊着昨夜没合上的文件。He left the letter on my desk.
sceneCN: 这里 desk 指「办公桌」（第 1 个义项：用于书写或办公的桌子）；句意是他把那封信留在了我的办公桌上。

senses.title: A table for working
senses.definition: a table with a flat top used for writing, reading or working
senses.definitionCN: 用于书写、阅读或工作的平顶桌子
senses.example: He left the letter on my desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那封信留在了我的办公桌上。
senses.why: A flat surface at the right height is the smallest office a person needs.
senses.whyCN: 一块高度合适的平面，就是一个人所需最小的办公室。

senses.title: A counter for service
senses.definition: a counter in a hotel or public building where people are helped
senses.definitionCN: 旅馆或公共建筑中为人提供帮助的柜台
senses.example: Please leave your key at the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 请把钥匙留在前台。
senses.why: The word for a work table slides easily to the place where work meets the public.
senses.whyCN: 工作桌这个词很容易滑向工作与公众相接的地方。

senses.title: A section of an office
senses.definition: a group in a newspaper or office that handles one kind of work
senses.definitionCN: 报社或机构中负责某一类工作的一组人
senses.example: She works on the sports desk of a daily paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家日报的体育部工作。
senses.why: A shared table becomes the name of the people gathered around it.
senses.whyCN: 一张共用的桌子，最后成了围坐者这一群人的名字。

intro.en: Desk goes back to Latin discus, a round plate, which became a table in Italian and medieval Latin before English borrowed it.
intro.cn: desk 可追到拉丁语 discus（圆盘），在意大利语与中世纪拉丁语中变成桌子，随后进入英语。

items.en: Discus meant a flat round object, a plate or a disc.
items.cn: discus 指扁圆的东西，盘子或圆盘。

items.en: Desca shifted from a plate to a board on legs for writing.
items.cn: desca 从盘子转指架在腿上或支架上的书写板。

items.en: Desco named a table, and travelers carried the word north.
items.cn: desco 指桌子，旅人把这个词带向北方。

items.en: English desk first meant a sloping reading stand.
items.cn: 英语里的 desk 最初指倾斜的读书架。

items.en: It grew drawers, then offices, then whole departments.
items.cn: 它后来长出抽屉，又指办公室，再指整个部门。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single sound, and the meaning group all name a flat surface people work or are served at.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音，近义组则都指人们工作或接受服务的平面。

entries.definition: a flat round object or storage device
a floor of a ship or a set of cards
entries.definitionCN: 船的一层甲板或一副牌

entries.definition: the top of a desk or a computer for a desk
a piece of furniture with a flat top
a long flat surface in a shop
a place set up for one person to work
entries.definitionCN: 为一人工作设置的工位

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with an elbow mark on wood and end with a whole department named after one table.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从木头上的一处手肘磨痕开始，落到以一个桌子命名的整个部门。

normal.en: A desk is a small stage where the day's work is performed.
normal.cn: 书桌是一个小舞台，一天的活儿在这里上演。

normal.en: The word once meant a plate, then a board, then a place to think.
normal.cn: 这个词先是盘子，再是板子，最后成了想事情的地方。

normal.en: The front desk is the table where the building meets its visitors.
normal.cn: 前台就是大楼接待来客的那张桌子。

normal.en: A tidy desk hides a busy week; a messy one tells the truth.
normal.cn: 整洁的桌子藏着忙碌的一周，凌乱的桌子说真话。

normal.en: Sit at the same desk long enough and it learns your shape.
normal.cn: 在同一张桌前坐得够久，它就会记住你的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a shallow dent worn into a wooden edge.
abstract.cn: 想象木桌边缘被磨出一处浅浅的凹痕。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp lighting only one sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照亮一张纸。

abstract.en: Picture a row of desks all facing the same wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一排桌子全都朝着同一面墙。

examples.en: He left the letter on my desk.
examples.cn: 他把那封信留在了我的办公桌上。

examples.en: Please leave your key at the front desk.
examples.cn: 请把钥匙留在前台。

examples.en: She works on the sports desk of a daily paper.
examples.cn: 她在一家日报的体育部工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desk 记成「得思考」：坐在桌前，就该得到一段安静思考的时间。

root: 来自拉丁语 discus（圆盘），经中世纪拉丁语 desca 与意大利语 desco（桌子）进入英语。本义是倾斜的读书架，后来指带抽屉的写字桌，又引申为旅馆前台与报社、机构里的部门。

sensesIntro.en: From a flat board for reading, to the counter of a hotel, to the people who share one table at work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块读书用的平板，到旅馆的柜台，再到工作时共用一张桌子的那群人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat surface at the height of a seated body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块与坐姿高度相合的平面。

branches.en: The first sense is the private table of one worker.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一个工作者私人的那张桌子。

branches.en: The second sense turns the table toward the public.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这张桌子转向公众。

branches.en: The third sense turns the table into a group of people.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把桌子变成了一群人。

branches.en: A desk and a front desk are the same furniture facing different ways.
branches.cn: 办公桌与前台是同一件家具，只是朝向不同。

branches.en: The counter that serves you and the desk that produces the paper are neighbours.
branches.cn: 接待你的柜台与编出报纸的部门，其实是邻居。

intro.en: Desk forms a small modern family about work done while sitting at a table.
intro.cn: desk 长出一小族现代词，都与坐在桌前完成的工作有关。

latinIntro.en: The oldest base is Latin discus, a flat round object, which turned into a table in medieval use.
latinIntro.cn: 最古老的词基是拉丁语 discus（扁圆物），在中世纪用法里转成了桌子。

items.example: The desk is by the window.
items.exampleCN: 书桌靠窗。
这间教室有三十张课桌。

items.meaning: the top of a desk, or a desk computer
items.example: The files sit on the desktop.
items.exampleCN: 文件放在桌面上。
他们换掉了旧台式电脑。

items.meaning: work done sitting at a desk
items.exampleCN: 案头工作让他背疼。

items.meaning: tied to a desk all day
items.exampleCN: 他觉得自己被桌子困住，坐立不安。

items.meaning: a worker who stays at an office desk
items.exampleCN: 内勤人员接了电话。

items.meaning: a small lamp for a desk
items.exampleCN: 把台灯打开。

definition_zh: 绝望；灰心；对……不再抱有希望
definition_en: a feeling that there is no hope at all
core_image: 一个人坐在熄了灯的房间地板上，背靠着门
scene: 连续几次面试都没有回音，他把简历扣在桌上不再去看。After months of failed attempts, he sank into despair.
sceneCN: 这里 despair 指「绝望」（第 1 个义项：完全看不到希望的感受）；句意是几个月尝试失败后，他陷入了绝望。

senses.title: No hope left at all
senses.definition: the feeling that there is no hope and nothing can be done
senses.definitionCN: 觉得毫无希望、无事可做的感受
senses.example: After months of failed attempts, he sank into despair.
senses.exampleCN: 几个月尝试失败后，他陷入了绝望。
senses.why: Despair is hope with the future switched off.
senses.whyCN: 绝望就是把未来的开关关掉之后的希望。

senses.title: Stop hoping for it
senses.definition: to stop hoping that something will happen or improve
senses.definitionCN: 不再希望某事发生或好转
senses.example: He despaired of ever finding a job in that town.
senses.exampleCN: 他对在那个镇上找到工作已不抱希望。
senses.why: The noun's feeling turns into a verb the moment it is aimed at one thing.
senses.whyCN: 当这种感受对准一件具体的事，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: The thing that defeats hope
senses.definition: a person or thing that makes other people feel hopeless
senses.definitionCN: 使别人感到毫无希望的人或事物
senses.example: The tangled wires were the despair of every repairman.
senses.exampleCN: 那团乱线是每个修理工的噩梦。
senses.why: Something so bad it defeats everyone ends up wearing the feeling it causes.
senses.whyCN: 糟糕到让所有人败下阵来的东西，最后会戴上它造成的感受。

intro.en: Despair comes from Latin desperare, to lose hope, built on de-, away, and sperare, to hope, from spes, hope.
intro.cn: despair 来自拉丁语 desperare（失去希望），由 de-（离开）与 sperare（希望）构成，后者源于 spes（希望）。

items.en: Spes was hope, and sperare meant to hope for something.
items.cn: spes 是希望，sperare 指对某事抱着希望。

items.en: De- reversed the verb, so desperare meant to hope no longer.
items.cn: de- 把这个动词反过来，desperare 就是不再抱有希望。

items.en: Desesperer kept the whole weight of the lost hope.
items.cn: desesperer 完整保留了失去希望的沉重感。

items.en: English used it as both a noun of feeling and a verb of giving up.
items.cn: 英语把它同时用作表示感受的名词与表示放弃的动词。

items.en: It can now even name a thing that defeats everyone who deals with it.
items.cn: 如今它甚至能指一件让所有接触者都束手无策的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sper root of hope, and the meaning group all sit close to hopelessness.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示希望的 sper 词基，近义组则都挨着「无望」这一带。

entries.definition: ready to try anything at all
the state of having no hope
showing that hope has gone
the feeling that nothing will improve
entries.definitionCN: 觉得一切都不会好转的感受

entries.definition: a dark and sad mood
calm acceptance of something bad

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a back against a closed door and end with a tangle of wires nobody can fix.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从背靠一扇关着的门开始，落到一团谁也理不清的乱线。

normal.en: Despair is hope that has stopped answering the door.
normal.cn: 绝望是希望不再来应门。

normal.en: De- takes the hope away and leaves the room empty.
normal.cn: de- 把希望拿走，房间就空了。

normal.en: The same word can be a feeling, an act and a thing.
normal.cn: 同一个词，可以是感受、是动作，也可以是一件东西。

normal.en: To despair of a town is to stop looking down its streets.
normal.cn: 对一座镇子绝望，就是不再朝它的街上张望。

normal.en: Some tasks are called the despair of workers because they beat everyone.
normal.cn: 有些活儿被叫作工人的噩梦，因为它们把每个人打败。

abstract.en: Picture a row of unopened letters on a dark table.
abstract.cn: 想象暗桌上摆着一排没拆的信。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that reaches for the phone and then stops.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向电话，又停住了。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the bulb has quietly gone out.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，灯泡悄悄熄了。

examples.en: After months of failed attempts, he sank into despair.
examples.cn: 几个月尝试失败后，他陷入了绝望。

examples.en: He despaired of ever finding a job in that town.
examples.cn: 他对在那个镇上找到工作已不抱希望。

examples.en: She looked at the broken machine in despair.
examples.cn: 她绝望地看着那台坏掉的机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 despair 记成「地死背儿」：de 是去掉，spair 像「希望」，希望被拿掉，只剩绝望。

root: 来自拉丁语 desperare（失去希望），由 de-（离开）与 sperare（希望）构成，sperare 又源于 spes（希望）。本义是把希望放走，后来指彻底看不到出路的感受，也可作动词表示不再指望，还指把人逼到无路可走的事物。

sensesIntro.en: From a feeling with no future, to the act of giving up on one thing, to a thing that makes everyone give up.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有未来的感受，到对某件事放弃期待的动作，再到让所有人都放弃的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room where the last lamp goes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮着的屋子，最后一盏灯灭了。

branches.en: The first sense is the darkness filling the whole room.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是黑暗填满整个房间。

branches.en: The second sense aims that darkness at one closed door.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把那片黑暗对准一扇关上的门。

branches.en: The third sense lets a thing carry the darkness for others.
branches.cn: 第三个义项让一件东西替别人背着那片黑暗。

branches.en: A mood and a decision differ only in how wide they reach.
branches.cn: 一种心境与一个决定，差别只在于波及多宽。

branches.en: What defeats many people becomes a byword for the feeling.
branches.cn: 让许多人败下阵来的东西，成了这种感受的代名词。

intro.en: Despair belongs to a Latin family built on hope, and its relatives spread from the feeling to the reckless act.
intro.cn: despair 属于一族建在「希望」上的拉丁词，同族词从这种感受延伸到不顾一切的行动。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin spes, hope; de- removes it, and the family keeps the same root in desperate and desperation.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 spes（希望），前缀 de- 把它拿走，desperate 与 desperation 沿用同一词根。

items.exampleCN: 不要太早绝望。
他对这个计划不再抱希望。
她发出一声绝望的叫喊。
他绝望地摇头。
他们拼死努力了一番。

items.example: She tried desperately to hold on.
items.exampleCN: 她拼命想抓住。

items.meaning: the state of having no hope
items.example: In desperation he sold the car.
items.exampleCN: 走投无路之下他卖掉了车。
她对这噪音已不抱希望。

definition_en: willing to try anything because you feel there is no other way
core_image: 一个人站在崖边，把最后一块木板推出去当作桥
scene: 最后一班车已经开走，他在雨里拦下每一辆经过的车。The stranded climbers made a desperate call for help.
sceneCN: 这里 desperate 指「拼命的」（第 1 个义项：因别无出路而不顾一切）；句意是被困的登山者拼命呼救。

senses.title: Ready to risk anything
senses.definition: willing to do something dangerous or extreme because no other choice seems open
senses.definitionCN: 因看不到别的出路而愿意做危险或极端的事
senses.example: The stranded climbers made a desperate call for help.
senses.exampleCN: 被困的登山者拼命呼救。
senses.why: When every road is closed, one road is chosen without counting the cost.
senses.whyCN: 当所有路都关着，人就会不计代价地选一条。

senses.title: Feeling no hope
senses.definition: feeling that there is no hope and no way out
senses.definitionCN: 觉得没有希望、也没有出路
senses.example: She felt desperate after the third rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次被拒之后，她感到绝望。
senses.why: The feeling and the act sit on the same day: first the dark, then the leap.
senses.whyCN: 感受与行动同处在一天里：先是黑下来，然后纵身一跳。

senses.title: Needing it very badly
senses.definition: needing something very much and having little of it
senses.definitionCN: 非常需要某物而手里几乎没有
senses.example: The team is desperate for a goalkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队急需一名守门员。
senses.why: A shortage sharpens want until it looks like hunger.
senses.whyCN: 短缺会把想要磨得锋利，直到它看起来像饥饿。

intro.en: Desperate comes from Latin desperatus, the past participle of desperare, to lose hope, from de- plus sperare, to hope.
intro.cn: desperate 来自拉丁语 desperatus，是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词，由 de- 与 sperare（希望）构成。

items.en: Desperatus described a person or case past all hope.
items.cn: desperatus 形容一个人或一件事已越过所有希望。

items.en: The word was used for the sick, the doomed and the reckless alike.
items.cn: 这个词既用于病人，也用于注定失败的人与不顾一切的人。

items.en: Desesperer gave the adjective its edge of violent effort.
items.cn: desesperer 给了这个形容词一股拼死用力的锋刃。

items.en: English applied it to acts, situations and needs.
items.cn: 英语把它用于行为、处境与需求。

items.en: The everyday sense softened into simply needing something badly.
items.cn: 日常用法又软化成「非常需要某物」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the same hope root, and the meaning group moves from no hope to urgent need.
note.cn: 形近组出自同一个表示希望的词根，近义组则从没有希望走到急迫的需要。

entries.definition: the feeling that no hope is left
the state of being ready to risk all
in a hopeless or frantic way
having no chance of success
wild with worry or fear
entries.definitionCN: 因担忧或恐惧而狂乱的

entries.definition: needing action right away

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin at the edge of a cliff and end with an empty goal mouth.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从悬崖边开始，落到一个空着的球门前。

normal.en: Desperate is what hope looks like when it starts running.
normal.cn: 绝望时的那种拼劲，就是希望开始狂奔的样子。

normal.en: When no road is open, people build one out of boards.
normal.cn: 没有路可走时，人们就用木板搭一条。

normal.en: The word can mean no hope, or simply no goalkeeper.
normal.cn: 这个词可以指毫无希望，也可以只指缺个守门员。

normal.en: De- plus sperare: hope taken away, effort left behind.
normal.cn: de- 加 sperare：希望被拿走，力气留在原地。

normal.en: A desperate measure is a measure taken by someone with no second plan.
normal.cn: 孤注一掷的手段，是没有第二套方案的人用的手段。

abstract.en: Picture a foot testing a plank over a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚在试一块横在空隙上的木板。

abstract.en: Picture two hands waving in the rain at a dark road.
abstract.cn: 想象雨中两双手朝一条黑路挥动。

abstract.en: Picture a goal with nobody standing in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有人站着的球门。

examples.en: The stranded climbers made a desperate call for help.
examples.cn: 被困的登山者拼命呼救。

examples.en: She felt desperate after the third rejection.
examples.cn: 第三次被拒之后，她感到绝望。

examples.en: The team is desperate for a goalkeeper.
examples.cn: 这支球队急需一名守门员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desperate 记成「地死怕他」：怕到极点，什么都不顾了，就是拼命。

root: 来自拉丁语 desperatus，是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词，由 de-（去掉）与 sperare（希望）构成。本义是希望已被耗尽，后来指无路可走时不顾一切的行动，也指心里彻底绝望，再由绝望引申为极度需要。

sensesIntro.en: From a leap taken with no second plan, to the dark feeling behind it, to a shortage that feels like hunger.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有退路时的一跃，到它背后的那片黑，再到像饥饿一样的短缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stepping onto a plank with nothing below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人踏上木板，脚下什么都没有。

branches.en: The first sense is the reckless step itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那不顾一切的一步。

branches.en: The second sense is the darkness that made the step possible.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是让这一步得以发生的那片黑。

branches.en: The third sense is a plain shortage pushing a person forward.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是推着人往前走的单纯短缺。

branches.en: Risk and despair are the outside and inside of one moment.

intro.en: Desperate shares the hope root with despair and grows forms for manner, state and reckless persons.
intro.cn: desperate 与 despair 共用表示希望的词根，并长出表示方式、状态与亡命之徒的形式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin spes, hope, and de- strips it away; -ate makes the result an adjective.

definition_en: in a way that shows no hope is left, or very much
core_image: 一个人用双手扒住最后一格台阶的边缘，指节发白
scene: 电话那头的人一遍遍重复同一个地址，声音越来越急。She searched desperately for the missing key.
sceneCN: 这里 desperately 指「拼命地」（第 1 个义项：用尽全力、不顾一切地）；句意是她拼命寻找那把丢失的钥匙。

senses.title: With every ounce of effort
senses.definition: with great effort because there seems to be no other hope
senses.definitionCN: 因似乎别无希望而用尽全力
senses.example: She searched desperately for the missing key.
senses.exampleCN: 她拼命寻找那把丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: The adverb turns a whole body into one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把整个身体拧成一个方向。

senses.title: With all hope gone
senses.definition: in a way that shows every hope has already been lost
senses.definitionCN: 以显示出所有希望都已失去的方式
senses.example: He looked desperately at the closed gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他绝望地看着那扇关上的大门。
senses.why: The same intensity can come from effort or from its failure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的强度，可以来自用力，也可以来自用力的失败。

senses.title: Very much indeed
senses.definition: used in everyday speech to mean very much
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中用来表示程度非常深
senses.example: She was desperately tired after the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班之后她累极了。
senses.why: Intensity borrowed from despair becomes a plain intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 从绝望那里借来的强度，最后成了一个普通的程度词。

intro.en: Desperately is desperate plus -ly, and desperate goes back to Latin desperatus, a person past all hope.
intro.cn: desperately 是 desperate 加 -ly，而 desperate 可追到拉丁语 desperatus，指已越过所有希望的人。

items.en: Desperatus was the past participle of desperare, to lose hope.
items.cn: desperatus 是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词。

items.en: The root spes, hope, is hidden inside the adverb still.
items.cn: 词根 spes（希望）至今仍藏在这个副词里。

items.en: The adverb appeared beside the adjective in written English.
items.cn: 这个副词在书面英语里与形容词一同出现。

items.en: It began to modify verbs of trying as well as verbs of feeling.
items.cn: 它开始修饰表示尝试的动词，而不只是表示感受的动词。

items.en: In speech it now simply means very, as in desperately tired.
items.cn: 在口语里它如今只表示非常，如累极了。

note.en: The look-alike group all share the hope root, and the meaning group runs from urgency to plain hopelessness.
note.cn: 形近组都共用表示希望的词根，近义组则从急迫一路走到彻底无望。

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从石阶上发白的指节开始，落到反复念着一个地址的声音。

normal.en: Desperately is desperate wearing an adverb's coat.

normal.en: The word still carries a hidden hope inside it.
normal.cn: 这个词里还藏着一个「希望」。

normal.en: When the hands pull hardest, the adverb shows up.
normal.cn: 双手最用劲的时候，这个副词就出现了。

normal.en: A tired adverb becomes a simple word for very.
normal.cn: 一个疲累的副词，最后成了「非常」的简单说法。

normal.en: Desperately poor and desperately late share one tone.
normal.cn: 极度贫困与急得迟到，用的是同一种口气。

abstract.cn: 想象手指扣住边沿，直到皮肤发白。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth saying the same street name again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴一遍遍念同一个街名。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who has stopped looking at the finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个已经不再看终点的奔跑者。

root: 由 desperate 加后缀 -ly 构成，desperate 则来自拉丁语 desperatus，是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词，词根为 spes（希望）。本义是以希望耗尽的方式做事，后来既指用尽全力，也指心里彻底无望，口语中又弱化为程度副词。

sensesIntro.en: From effort at full strength, to the look of lost hope, to a casual word for very.
sensesIntro.cn: 从全力使出的劲，到失去希望的神色，再到口语里表示非常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers holding on with the last of their strength.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指用最后一点力气扣住不放。

branches.en: The first sense is strength pushed to its limit.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是力气被推到极限。

branches.en: The second sense is the face after the limit is passed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是越过极限之后的那张脸。

branches.en: The third sense is the same force worn down into emphasis.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是同一股力道被磨成了强调。

branches.en: Effort and hopelessness are two readings of the same tight grip.
branches.cn: 用力与绝望，是同一只紧握的手的两种读法。

branches.en: A word for survival effort can end up meaning merely very tired.
branches.cn: 一个表示求生力气的词，最后可以只表示累得不行。

intro.en: Desperately belongs to the hope family and adds the ending that turns it into a manner word.
intro.cn: desperately 属于「希望」这一族，加上后缀后成为一个表示方式的词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin spes, hope, with de- removing it and -ly marking the adverb in English.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 spes（希望），de- 把它移走，英语再用 -ly 标出副词。

definition_en: used to say that something happens even though another thing could have stopped it
core_image: 雨水顺着伞骨往下淌，伞下的人仍旧往前走
scene: 风把海报吹得翻卷起来，来听讲座的人还是坐满了屋子。Despite the heavy rain, the whole class came on time.
sceneCN: 这里 despite 指「尽管」（第 1 个义项：表示某事没有被另一情况阻止）；句意是尽管下着大雨，全班还是准时到了。

senses.title: It happened anyway
senses.definition: used before a noun to show that something did not prevent an action
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示某情况并未阻止某个动作
senses.example: Despite the heavy rain, the whole class came on time.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下着大雨，全班还是准时到了。
senses.why: One force pushes, and the thing still moves the other way.
senses.whyCN: 一股力量推过来，那件事却仍旧朝另一边走。

senses.title: Against someone's wishes
senses.definition: used before a noun to show that an action goes against what someone wants or feels
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示某行为违背某人的意愿或情感
senses.example: Despite his family's wishes, he left the farm for the city.
senses.exampleCN: 不顾家人的意愿，他离开农场去了城市。
senses.why: The word once meant looking down on someone, and a trace of that refusal remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从前指俯视某人，那种不理会至今还留着一丝痕迹。

intro.en: Despite came from Old French despit, contempt, from Latin despectus, a looking down on, built on de- and specere, to look.
intro.cn: despite 来自古法语 despit（轻蔑），源于拉丁语 despectus（俯视），由 de- 与 specere（看）构成。

items.en: Specere meant to look, and despicere meant to look down on.
items.cn: specere 指看，despicere 指往下看、瞧不起。

items.en: Despectus named the contempt itself.
items.cn: despectus 指的就是这种轻蔑本身。

items.en: Despit carried both scorn and the phrase in despite of.
items.cn: despit 既带着蔑视，也带着 in despite of 这个说法。

items.en: English shortened the phrase until despite stood alone as a preposition.
items.cn: 英语把这个短语越缩越短，最后 despite 独自成了介词。

items.en: The scorn faded, leaving only the sense of something not stopping you.
items.cn: 轻蔑的色彩淡去，只留下「某事拦不住你」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spit or spect shape, and the meaning group all mark a contrast that did not change the result.
note.cn: 形近组共用 spit 或 spect 的形状，近义组则都标记一种没能改变结果的对照。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with rain running off an umbrella and end with a family waving goodbye at a gate.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从雨水顺着伞骨往下淌开始，落到门口挥手告别的家人。

normal.en: Despite sets up a wall and then walks straight through it.
normal.cn: despite 先砌一堵墙，然后径直穿过去。

normal.en: The word once meant looking down, so it still refuses to bow.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指往下看，所以至今也不肯低头。

normal.en: Despite takes a noun; although takes a whole sentence.
normal.cn: despite 后面接名词，although 后面接一整句。

normal.en: Rain, warnings, wishes: all can follow despite and change nothing.
normal.cn: 雨、警告、家人的意愿，都能跟在 despite 后面，却什么也改变不了。

normal.en: Despite everything is what people say when they are still standing.
normal.cn: 还站着的人，才会说 despite everything。

abstract.en: Picture an umbrella bent forward against a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一把伞顶着大风向前倾。

abstract.en: Picture wet footprints leading into a dry hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一串湿脚印一直通向干燥的大厅。

abstract.en: Picture a packed room while the storm hits the windows.
abstract.cn: 想象窗外风雨拍打，屋里却坐满了人。

examples.en: Despite the heavy rain, the whole class came on time.
examples.cn: 尽管下着大雨，全班还是准时到了。

examples.en: Despite his family's wishes, he left the farm for the city.
examples.cn: 不顾家人的意愿，他离开农场去了城市。

examples.en: The plan failed despite all their efforts.
examples.cn: 尽管他们尽了全力，计划还是失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 despite 记成「地死拜特」：de 是去掉，spite 是阻碍，阻碍被去掉，事情照做，就是尽管。

root: 来自古法语 despit（轻蔑），源于拉丁语 despectus（俯视），由 de-（向下）与 specere（看）构成。本义是瞧不起、不放在眼里，短语 in despite of 逐渐缩成介词，表示某情况存在却没能阻止某事，也指不顾某人的意愿。

sensesIntro.en: From a look of contempt, to a preposition that lets an obstacle stand and then walks past it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从轻蔑的一瞥，到一个先让障碍站着、再从旁边走过去的介词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an obstacle standing still while the action passes it.
core.cn: 核心意象：障碍站着不动，行动却从旁边过去了。

branches.en: The first sense is an obstacle that fails to stop anything.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一个没能拦住任何事的障碍。

branches.en: The second sense is a person's wish treated the same way.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是某人的意愿被同样对待。

branches.en: Rain, cost and distance are the usual things it stands before.
branches.cn: 雨、代价与距离，是它最常挡在前面的东西。

branches.en: A storm and a family's advice both count as things not listened to.
branches.cn: 一场暴雨与家人的劝告，都算作没被听从的东西。

branches.en: The old contempt survives only as this quiet refusal to yield.
branches.cn: 古老的轻蔑只剩下这一点安静的、不肯让步。

intro.en: Despite is tied to a family of looking down and of spite, which still colours the modern preposition.
intro.cn: despite 与一族表示俯视和怨恨的词相连，这层色彩至今还在影响这个介词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin specere, to look; de- points the look downward, and despicere means to scorn.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 specere（看），de- 把目光转向下方，despicere 就是轻视。

items.exampleCN: 尽管很冷，他们还是出门了。

items.example: He said it out of spite.

definition_en: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
core_image: 正餐的盘子被收走，一小碟冰淇淋放到桌上，勺子还冒着凉气
scene: 服务员收走主菜的盘子，又端来一小碟淋了果酱的布丁。We had apple pie for dessert.

senses.title: Sweet food after a meal

senses.example: We had apple pie for dessert.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃了苹果派当甜点。
senses.why: The meal ends, and the mouth asks for one last pleasant thing.
senses.whyCN: 一餐结束了，嘴还想再要一件让人愉快的东西。

senses.title: The sweet course itself
senses.definition: the course at the end of a formal dinner, served with its own dishes
senses.definitionCN: 正式宴席末端的一道，配有自己的餐具
senses.example: The dessert came with a small glass of sweet wine.
senses.exampleCN: 甜点环节配了一小杯甜酒。
senses.why: A course is not just food; it has its own plates and its own moment.
senses.whyCN: 一道菜不只是食物，它有自己的盘子和自己的时刻。

intro.en: Dessert comes from French desservir, to clear the table, built on des-, un-, and servir, to serve.
intro.cn: dessert 来自法语 desservir（撤去餐具），由 des-（去除）与 servir（上菜、服务）构成。

items.en: Desservir meant to remove what had been served.
items.cn: desservir 指把已经上过的东西撤走。

items.en: Dessert named what came after the clearing, the last sweet course.
items.cn: dessert 指撤桌之后端上来的东西，也就是最后那道甜食。

items.en: English borrowed dessert for the fruit and sweets ending a dinner.
items.cn: 英语借来 dessert，指结束一顿晚餐的水果与甜食。

items.en: Sugar and cheap ovens turned it into cakes and ices.
items.cn: 糖与便宜烤炉让它变成蛋糕和冰品。

items.en: The single s in the middle still separates it from a dry desert.
items.cn: 中间那个单独的 s，至今把它与干旱的沙漠分开。

note.en: The look-alike group is the famous one-s and two-s trap, and the meaning group gathers sweet endings to a meal.
note.cn: 形近组就是那个著名的一个 s 与两个 s 的陷阱，近义组则聚起一餐的甜味收尾。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a cleared dinner plate and end with the feeling of one last sweet bite.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从收空的餐盘开始，落到最后一口甜味的感觉。

normal.en: Two s for the sweet, one s for the sand.
normal.cn: 甜的那个有两个 s，沙的那个只有一个。

normal.en: Dessert is literally the food that arrives after the table is cleared.
normal.cn: dessert 字面上就是撤桌之后才到的那份食物。

normal.en: A desert has no water; a dessert needs no water at all.
normal.cn: 沙漠缺水，甜点则根本用不着水。

normal.en: The last course is the one the meal remembers.
normal.cn: 最后一道菜，往往是一顿饭记得最久的那道。

normal.en: Say the word slowly and the double s keeps the sweetness in.

abstract.en: Picture a small dish set down where the main plate had been.

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifting one cold, dark curl of chocolate.
abstract.cn: 想象一把匙舀起一小卷冰凉的深色巧克力。

abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛还亮着，旁边是空掉的咖啡杯。

examples.en: We had apple pie for dessert.
examples.cn: 我们吃了苹果派当甜点。

examples.en: The dessert came with a small glass of sweet wine.

examples.en: She ordered two desserts because she could not choose.
examples.cn: 她点了两份甜点，因为实在选不出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dessert 记成「地舌特」：两个 s 像两勺糖，糖多的那个才是甜点。

root: 来自法语 desservir（撤去餐具），由 des-（去除）与 servir（上菜）构成。本义是撤桌之后端上来的东西，后来专指正餐末尾的甜食与甜点那一道，中间两个 s 的拼写也成了它与沙漠的区别。

sensesIntro.en: From the food brought after the plates are cleared, to the ritual course that ends a formal dinner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从撤盘之后端来的食物，到正式宴席末尾那一道仪式性的甜点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sweet dish placed where the main plate was.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小甜碟放在原来主菜盘的位置。

branches.en: The first sense is simply the sweet food at the end.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是结尾那份甜的食物。

branches.en: The second sense is that food raised into a formal course.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这份食物被抬成正式的一道。

branches.en: Pie, ice and fruit all count as this closing sweetness.
branches.cn: 派、冰品与水果，都算作这种收尾的甜。

branches.en: Everyday dinners and state banquets both end on the same note.
branches.cn: 家常晚饭与国宴，都以同一个音收尾。

branches.en: A course brings its own spoon, its own plate and its own pause.
branches.cn: 一道菜自带它的匙、它的盘与它的停顿。

intro.en: Dessert forms a small family of dishes and spoons used at the sweet end of a meal.
intro.cn: dessert 长出一小族词，都与一餐甜味收尾时的餐具和食物有关。

latinIntro.en: The base is French servir, to serve, and des- means the serving is taken away again.

definition_en: the place that someone or something is travelling to
core_image: 长途车窗外的路牌，一个地名后面跟着一支箭头
scene: 大巴在夜里开了很久，司机终于报出那个熟悉的地名。After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.

senses.title: The place you are going to
senses.definition: the place that a person or vehicle is travelling toward
senses.definitionCN: 人或车辆正在前往的那个地方
senses.example: After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.
senses.exampleCN: 在路上走了十个小时后，他们到达了目的地。
senses.why: A journey needs one fixed point for every turn to point at.
senses.whyCN: 一段旅程需要一个固定的点，让每一次转弯都有所指。

senses.title: The end of the line
senses.definition: the final stop on a route or transport service
senses.definitionCN: 某条路线或交通线路的最后一站
senses.example: This train's destination is the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟列车的终点是海边。
senses.why: Tracks end somewhere, and the map must name that end.
senses.whyCN: 轨道总在某处结束，地图必须给那个结束命名。

senses.title: A place people travel to
senses.definition: a place that many people choose to visit for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 许多人为了游玩而选择前往的地方
senses.example: The old port is now a favourite destination for divers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧港口如今是潜水者喜爱的去处。
